cells.verb: still hoping for it after everything that's happened
cells.place: in the tending of something that isn't finished yet
cells.ask: If you want somewhere for that to go: let it harden into something practical. Hold the thing steady when the ground gets hard — not gripping it, just not leaving — and what you've been tending gets to finish on its own time and shine because it actually did.
cells.core:
You're still hoping for what's growing, and the hope has been tested enough that it isn't naive anymore. You've seen it almost not make it, more than once, and you kept tending anyway — not because you were sure, because you weren't done. That kind of hoping is load-bearing. It's the thing the growing is leaning on while it figures itself out.
If you want somewhere for that to go: let it harden into something practical. Hold the thing steady when the ground gets hard — not gripping it, just not leaving — and what you've been tending gets to finish on its own time and shine because it actually did.
cells.sheetLine: You've kept hoping through the hard parts, and it's holding something up.

cells.tense: Future — bracing at a harvest that hasn't happened.
cells.verb: hoping so hard it's become steering
cells.place: over something that's still deciding what it is
cells.ask: What might help is the opposite of hoping harder: look at what's actually in front of you before you say what it'll become. Let yourself not know for a while — the knowing that's accurate tends to arrive quietly, without needing you to argue for it. Then the thing gets to shine because it finished, not because you believed it would.
cells.core:
You're hoping for what's growing so hard that the hope has started doing the growing's job. You can already see where it ends up, and you're tending toward that picture — reaching ahead of what's actually there, adjusting it toward the version you've decided on. The faith is real. It's just running out in front of the thing it's supposed to be holding.
What might help is the opposite of hoping harder: look at what's actually in front of you before you say what it'll become. Let yourself not know for a while — the knowing that's accurate tends to arrive quietly, without needing you to argue for it. Then the thing gets to shine because it finished, not because you believed it would.
cells.sheetLine: You've decided how it ends, and you're tending toward the ending instead of the thing.

cells.tense: Past — standing where the hope got left, not where the growing is.
cells.verb: going through the motions of hoping without the hope in it
cells.place: beside something that could still grow if someone believed it might
cells.ask: Don't try to make yourself hope again — that doesn't take. Instead, do one plain act of tending, with care and without needing to believe first: show up for it, give it what it needs today, and leave the outcome alone. Hope tends to come back through the hands. And when the thing finishes, it shines because it was cared for the whole way.
cells.core:
The hoping isn't in the room with you. You might still be tending — watering, showing up, doing what the thing needs — but the expectation that it'll come to anything is somewhere behind you, and the care is arriving without it. The thing can feel that. What's growing isn't short on attention. It's short on anyone in the room believing it will get to finish.
Don't try to make yourself hope again — that doesn't take. Instead, do one plain act of tending, with care and without needing to believe first: show up for it, give it what it needs today, and leave the outcome alone. Hope tends to come back through the hands. And when the thing finishes, it shines because it was cared for the whole way.
cells.sheetLine: You're still tending it. The hope isn't in the room with you.

cells.tense: Disowned present — you're the one holding it up and calling it luck.
cells.verb: keeping hope alive without saying so
cells.place: around something that's only still growing because you didn't give up on it
cells.ask: What might help is to say the simpler thing underneath: not that you believed, but that you held on when it was hard. That's a plain fact, and it's yours. Once it's yours, the hope on top of it is too — and the thing you've been keeping alive gets to shine as something you actually grew.
cells.core:
You've been hoping for this through every hard stretch — it's why it's still here — but ask you and you'd say it just made it on its own, or that you got lucky, or that it was never really in your hands. The persistence is running. It's steering what you do every day. The one person who won't credit it is you.
What might help is to say the simpler thing underneath: not that you believed, but that you held on when it was hard. That's a plain fact, and it's yours. Once it's yours, the hope on top of it is too — and the thing you've been keeping alive gets to shine as something you actually grew.
cells.sheetLine: It's still alive because you never stopped hoping. You call that luck.
